# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 11 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 11 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_011_page_001.jpg

---

**11:1** She prospered their works through the hand of a holy prophet.

**11:2** They journeyed through a trackless wilderness and pitched their camps in uncharted regions.

**11:3** They withstood enemies and beat back their foes.

**11:4** When they were thirsty, they called upon you, and water was given to them from a sheer rock, and a remedy for their thirst from hard stone.

**11:5** For the very things by which their enemies were punished became in their need a benefit to them.

**11:6** Instead of the ever-flowing source of a river, befouled with blood as a rebuke to the decree of infanticide,

**11:7** you gave them abundant water when they least expected it,

**11:8** showing by the thirst they had endured at that time how you had punished their adversaries.

**11:9** For when they were tested — even while being disciplined in mercy — they understood how the ungodly were being tormented when judged in wrath.

**11:10** For these you tested, admonishing them as a father; but those you examined, condemning them as a stern king.

**11:11** Whether absent or present, they were equally distressed;

**11:12** for a twofold grief held them, and a groaning as they remembered what had been.

**11:13** For when they heard that through their own punishments the others had been benefited, they recognized the Lord.

**11:14** For one whom long ago they had mocked and rejected, at the outcome of events they came to marvel at — having thirsted in a different way than the righteous had.

**11:15** In return for the foolish counsels of their unrighteousness — by which they were led astray to worship irrational reptiles and worthless vermin — you sent upon them a great multitude of irrational creatures as punishment,

**11:16** so that they might know that one is punished by the very things through which one sins.

**11:17** For your all-powerful hand, which created the world from formless matter, was not without the means to send upon them a multitude of bears or fierce lions,

**11:18** or newly created and unknown fierce beasts, full of rage, either breathing a fiery blast, or belching forth a roar of smoke, or shooting terrible sparks from their eyes,

**11:19** whose power to harm could not only have destroyed them, but whose terrifying appearance alone could have killed them.

**11:20** Even apart from all this, they could have been struck down by a single breath, pursued by justice and scattered by the breath of your power. But you have ordered all things by measure and number and weight.

**11:21** For it is always within your power to show great strength, and who can withstand the might of your arm?

**11:22** Because before you the whole world is like a grain on the scales of a balance, and like a drop of morning dew fallen upon the earth.

**11:23** But you have mercy on all, because you are able to do all things, and you overlook the sins of human beings for the sake of repentance.

**11:24** For you love all things that exist, and you loathe nothing that you have made; for you would not have fashioned anything if you had hated it.

**11:25** And how would anything have endured unless you had willed it? Or how would anything have been preserved unless called into being by you?

**11:26** But you spare all, because they are yours, O Master, lover of souls.
